basic_information.official_title: AN ACT GOVERNING THE OBSERVANCE OF REGULAR AND SPECIAL HOLIDAYS IN THE BANGSAMORO AUTONOMOUS REGION IN MUSLIM MINDANAO (BARMM), REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE MUSLIM MINDANAO AUTONOMY ACT NO. 17
signed_by: Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: 15 days after completion of publication in the Bangsamoro Gazette or at least one newspaper of general circulation in the BARMM

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Sets the region's own holidays — which days are non-working, which are working, and who declares them — and confirms that private sector workers get national holiday pay rules until the region writes its own labour code.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: To replace the old ARMM holiday law with one that recognises the Bangsamoro's own history and religious calendar, upholds workers' rights and well-being, and keeps the regional economy competitive.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: Four regular non-working holidays and two special non-working holidays are fixed, alongside nine special working holidays. The Chief Minister must publish next year's holidays by 31 December each year, and Islamic dates are set on the Grand Mufti's recommendation.
who_will_be_affected: Every private sector worker and employer in the BARMM
All regional government branches, agencies and local government units
BARMM offices located outside the region, which are also covered
Anyone whose legal deadline falls on a holiday
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: In force since 2023 — 15 days after completion of publication.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: NOW LAW. The region has its own holidays. Four are regular non-working days, two more are special non-working, and nine are working holidays. Private sector holiday pay follows the national Labor Code until the Bangsamoro writes its own.
in_practice: Regular non-working holidays: Bangsamoro Foundation Day (21 January), Eid'l Fit'r (Shawwal 1), Eid'l Adha (Dhul Hijja 10), Day of Shuhada (18 March)
Special non-working holidays: Day of Arafah (Dhul Hijja 9) and the 1st Day of Tashriq (Dhul Hijja 11)

Special working holidays include Bangsamoro Day of Solidarity (1 February), Battle of Bud Daho Day (6 March), the Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro signing (27 March), Battle of Bayang Day (2 May), the MNLF–OIC–GRP 1996 Final Peace Agreement and 1976 Tripoli Agreement (2 September), Shiek Karimul Makhdum Day (7 November), Shariff Kabunsuan Day (19 December), and Bangsamoro Indigenous Peoples' Thanksgiving Day
The Chief Minister issues a proclamation on or before 31 December each year listing the next year's holidays
Islamic holiday dates follow the Grand Mufti of the Bangsamoro Darul Ifta's recommendation
If a legal deadline falls on a holiday, the act may be done on the next business day

for_specific_groups.Private sector workers: You are covered — Section 4 binds the private sector, and Section 12 applies the national Labor Code's holiday compensation rules until a Bangsamoro Labor Code exists.
for_specific_groups.Employers: Holidays under this act must be officially observed by the private sector as well as by government.
for_specific_groups.BARMM staff posted outside the region: Section 4 covers BARMM offices located outside its territorial jurisdiction.
for_specific_groups.Local governments: You can endorse a founding-anniversary holiday by council resolution, and must give the Chief Minister's office at least 15 days' notice.
for_specific_groups.Indigenous Peoples: Bangsamoro Indigenous Peoples' Thanksgiving Day is a special working holiday, set on the day the IP Code is enacted.
for_specific_groups.Anyone with a filing deadline: Section 13 lets you do it on the next business day if the deadline falls on a holiday.

what_this_means_for_you.where_this_applies: The BARMM, its constituent LGUs, and BARMM offices outside the region.
what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: Every year — the Chief Minister's proclamation is due by 31 December for the following year.
what_you_can_do: Look for the Chief Minister's annual proclamation, due on or before 31 December, for next year's dates
Check whether a day is working or non-working — the proclamation must say which
If you are in the private sector, holiday pay follows the national Labor Code rules
Ask your LGU to endorse a local founding-anniversary holiday by resolution
watch_out_for: Special *working* holidays are commemorations, not days off — most of the historical dates fall in this category.
Islamic holidays move with the Hijri calendar, so the exact date each year comes from the Grand Mufti's recommendation and the Chief Minister's proclamation.
A special non-working holiday must be proclaimed at least 5 days before the date, and endorsements need 15 days' notice.
The act sets no penalty for an employer who fails to observe a holiday; enforcement runs through labour law.

key_terms_explained.Regular non-working holiday: A day off observed throughout the region, with national and regional holidays provided by law.
key_terms_explained.Special working holiday: A commemorative day that is still a working day.
key_terms_explained.Grand Mufti: The highest authority of the Bangsamoro Darul Ifta', who recommends the actual dates of Islamic holidays.
key_terms_explained.Pretermission: Moving an act to the next business day when its deadline falls on a holiday.
key_terms_explained.PD 1083: The Code on Muslim Personal Laws of the Philippines, whose other holidays are treated as special working holidays.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed Muharram 02, 1445 / 20 July 2023, approved by the Chief Minister on 17 August 2023.

benefits.headline: The region's own holiday calendar, with national holiday pay rules confirmed for private sector workers.

direct_benefits.benefit: Four regular non-working holidays and two special non-working holidays
direct_benefits.who_gets_it: Workers across the region, public and private
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Observed automatically; dates confirmed in the annual proclamation

direct_benefits.benefit: Holiday compensation under the national Labor Code
direct_benefits.who_gets_it: Private sector employees in the BARMM
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Section 12, pending a Bangsamoro Labor Code

direct_benefits.benefit: An annual published list of next year's holidays
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Chief Minister's proclamation, due on or before 31 December

direct_benefits.benefit: Extra time when a deadline falls on a holiday
direct_benefits.who_gets_it: Anyone with a legal filing deadline

indirect_benefits: Funded commemorative activities — ministries, agencies and LGUs must allocate funds for them
A route for localities to have their founding anniversary proclaimed
limitations: Most historical commemorations are working holidays, not days off.
No penalty in this act for non-observance.
Islamic dates are not fixed in advance in the act itself.

for_employers: Officially observe the holidays provided under the act
Apply national Labor Code holiday compensation rules to private sector employees
for_government_and_lgus: Allocate funds and conduct activities commemorating the holidays
Give the Chief Minister's office at least 15 days' notice with a certified copy of any endorsing resolution

what_is_prohibited: The act defines no prohibited acts and creates no offences.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence, fine or imprisonment.
penalties.note: Holiday pay obligations on private employers are enforced through the Labor Code of the Philippines, which Section 12 applies pending a Bangsamoro Labor Code.

where_to_complain.first_stop: Office of the Chief Minister, which proclaims the holidays
where_to_complain.for_pay_disputes: Labour authorities applying the Labor Code of the Philippines, per Section 12
where_to_complain.for_local_holidays: Bangsamoro Commission for the Preservation of Cultural Heritage, which recommends localized proclamations
where_to_complain.note: The act creates no complaints procedure of its own.

everyday_scenarios: A shop worker in Cotabato City works on Eid'l Fit'r. That is a regular non-working holiday, and holiday compensation follows the national Labor Code under Section 12.

A municipality wants its founding anniversary declared a special non-working holiday. Its Sangguniang Bayan passes a resolution, endorses it to the Chief Minister, and the office must have notice and a certified copy at least 15 days before the date.
A permit application is due on the Day of Shuhada. Section 13 lets it be filed on the next business day.
A family plans around Eid'l Adha. The exact date follows the Hijri calendar, recommended by the Grand Mufti and confirmed in the Chief Minister's annual proclamation issued by 31 December.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Short title: the “Bangsamoro Holidays Act of 2023”.

Section 2 — Policy: recognise regional and local public holidays preserving the history, tradition and cultural heritage of the Bangsamoro and other peoples in the BARMM, reflective of their system of life as prescribed by their faith; uphold the rights and well-being of workers; and promote the vibrance and competitiveness of the regional economy.

Section 3 — Defines regular non-working holidays as national and regional holidays provided by law observed throughout the area of autonomy, and special holidays as non-regular holidays in the region and certain LGUs marking historical, religious and other significant events. Special holidays may be classified as working or non-working days.

Section 4 — Coverage: holidays under the act are officially observed by the private sector and by all branches, subdivisions, instrumentalities and agencies of the regional government including constituent LGUs, and by all BARMM offices located outside its territorial jurisdiction.

Section 5 — Regular non-working holidays: Bangsamoro Foundation Day (21 January), Eid'l Fit'r (Shawwal 1), Eid'l Adha (Dhul Hijja 10) and the Day of Shuhada (18 March). Special non-working holidays: the Day of Arafah (Dhul Hijja 9) and the 1st Day of Tashriq (Dhul Hijja 11). Special working holidays: holidays under Presidential Decree 1083 other than those named here, Bangsamoro Day of Solidarity (1 February), Battle of Bud Daho Day (6 March), the signing of the Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro (27 March), Battle of Bayang Day (2 May), Shiek Karimul Makhdum Day (7 November), Shariff Kabunsuan Day (19 December), the signing of the MNLF–OIC–GRP 1996 Final Peace Agreement and 1976 Tripoli Agreement (2 September), and Bangsamoro Indigenous Peoples' Thanksgiving Day on the day of the enactment of the IP Code. The Chief Minister may modify actual dates of observance by proclamation.
Section 6 — The Grand Mufti of the Bangsamoro Darul Ifta' recommends to the Chief Minister the actual dates for declaring Islamic holidays based on the Hijri calendar.

Section 7 — Days of historical significance to specific LGUs may be proclaimed special non-working holidays in that locality by the Chief Minister, on the recommendation of the Bangsamoro Commission for the Preservation of Cultural Heritage, which formulates guidelines; LGUs submit proposals at least 15 days before.
Section 8 — All ministries, agencies, offices and instrumentalities, including LGUs, shall allocate funds and conduct activities commemorating the holidays.

Sections 9–10 — Regional and local special holidays require official proclamation by the Chief Minister stating whether they are working or non-working. Parliament or the relevant local council may endorse by resolution; the Office of the Chief Minister must receive notice and a certified copy at least 15 calendar days before, and any proclamation of a special non-working holiday must be made at least 5 days before the date.
Section 11 — The Chief Minister shall issue a proclamation on or before 31 December each year declaring the regular and special holidays to be observed in the next succeeding year.
Section 12 — Pending enactment of a Bangsamoro Labor Code, the holiday compensation provisions of the Labor Code of the Philippines apply to private sector employees within the BARMM.
Section 13 — Where the day, or last day, for performing any act required or permitted by law falls on a regular or special holiday, the act may be done on the next succeeding business day.
Section 15 — Repeals Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 17 and all other regional issuances pertaining to regional holidays.
Section 16 — Takes effect 15 days after completion of publication in the Bangsamoro Gazette or at least one newspaper of general circulation.

who_benefits: Local communities marking their own histories

citizen_questions.q: Which days are actual days off?
citizen_questions.a: Four regular non-working holidays — Bangsamoro Foundation Day (21 January), Eid'l Fit'r, Eid'l Adha and the Day of Shuhada (18 March) — plus two special non-working holidays, the Day of Arafah and the 1st Day of Tashriq.

citizen_questions.q: Are the historical commemorations days off?
citizen_questions.a: Mostly no. Bud Daho, Bayang, the Comprehensive Agreement signing, the 1996 Final Peace Agreement and the rest are special *working* holidays — commemorated, but still working days.

citizen_questions.q: Do private companies have to follow this?
citizen_questions.a: Yes. Section 4 says holidays under the act are officially observed by the private sector as well as by government.
Pending a Bangsamoro Labor Code, Section 12 applies the holiday compensation provisions of the Labor Code of the Philippines to private sector employees in the region.

citizen_questions.q: How do I know the exact dates each year?
citizen_questions.a: The Chief Minister must issue a proclamation on or before 31 December each year listing the next year's holidays. Islamic dates follow the Grand Mufti's recommendation under the Hijri calendar.

citizen_questions.q: What if a legal deadline lands on a holiday?
citizen_questions.a: Section 13 lets the act be done on the next succeeding business day.

citizen_questions.q: Can my town have its own holiday?
citizen_questions.a: Yes. A local council can endorse its founding anniversary by resolution to the Chief Minister, with at least 15 days' notice, and days of local historical significance can be proclaimed on the cultural heritage commission's recommendation.
